label: Claude Opus 5.5 (Agency native)
explanation: Diagnosis: with thinking on, unedited Qwen3.5-0.8B almost never closes its thinking. 31/32 problems were truncated at 16k tokens (1/32 correct), and 27/32 at 8k. The cause is runaway self-doubt loops: "Wait" starts most lines (about 9.7k of them in 32 replies), and token entropy drops to about 0.001 once a loop sets in. The same problems in non-thinking mode were about 55-60% correct, and every thinking run that did close was correct, so the main loss is failing to terminate. Edit: a rank-2 LoRA on model.layers.23.mlp.down_proj (||dW||/||W|| = 0.056). Because it is the last sublayer, the edit only changes output logits and leaves internal states untouched. Read side (A): (1) a near-constant input direction (ridge least-squares onto 1; held-out mean about 1.0, sd about 0.03, about 0.9 in chat); (2) a ridge-regressed log-position direction (held-out correlation about 0.7) that rises with reasoning length and in loops. Write side (B): minimum-norm residual vectors, built through the final norm and tied unembedding, that raise the </think> logit by about 5.5 + 2*(logpos - 6.5) nats at T=1 (about +1 at the end of the prompt, about 4-6 early in the reply, about 11 deep in loops), with no change to <|im_end|>, <think> and other special or newline tokens. A second vector suppresses Wait/ wait by about 3 nats, with alternatives like So/Let/If/But held fixed. Offline hazard estimates on the unedited model's own trajectories, using the eval's sampling settings (T=0.6, top-k 20, top-p 0.95, presence penalty), suggest thinking now ends within about 1-7k tokens, with almost no chance of ending at the first token. Spurious </think> in short non-thinking chat is about 0. These are static estimates, and the edited model was never run.
